title: Minimax Deployment Regret for Low-Tucker-Rank Bernoulli Response Tensors with Unknown Axes
banked_reason: D0.5.G tier=subfield < floor=field; paper_score_ceiling 6.8 < 7.4. Not salvageable within scope: sound matched minimax frontier, but attaining procedure lacks usable traffic calibration and scope is narrow.
gap_reasons: The principal significance constraint is the attaining procedure: it defaults to one arm until n/d reaches 2^512 and then uses enormous confidence-box enumeration, so the package supplies a statistical rate without usable experimental traffic calibration.
The oracle premium compares worst-case minimax risks and does not establish an instance-specific cost of learning axes.
The square, three-mode, exact-rank-two benchmark and absence of an implementable supporting example limit the leading-journal case despite the completed frontier.
proof_attempt_summary: The discovery graph derives matching logarithm-free lower and upper bounds for the unchanged unknown-axis class, using legal strong-signal alternatives and a total exact-budget design. A same-class known-axis benchmark and matching minimax premium were added after maximality review, and the math and decision panels passed with six cited leaves attested. The field claim failed on practical calibration and narrow scope rather than mathematical correctness; the run stopped before Lean formalization.
tldr: The all-budget minimax causal deployment regret on the complete stated class of unknown Tucker-rank-two Bernoulli response tensors is \(\Theta(\min\{1,\sqrt{d/n}\})\), with no necessary logarithmic factor. A total original-record experiment attains this frontier without latent side information or selected-subtensor conditioning. If the three mode column spaces are revealed before the same \(n\)-record experiment, the risk is instead \(\Theta(\min\{1,n^{-1/2}\})\). Their ratio is \(\Theta(\sqrt{\min\{n,d\}})\): learning unknown axes costs \(\Theta(\sqrt d)\) in the precision regime \(n\ge d\), with smaller-budget saturation accounted for explicitly. Both frontiers allow exact policy ties.
gap: The closest terminal factorial result maintains conditional completion and regularity on successively restricted tensors. The inspected reconstruction and known-feature exploration theorems do not identify the complete original-class, all-budget deployment frontier.
fill: A single matched minimax result must combine legal adaptive alternatives and a total original-record design, resolving policy-specific confidence error rather than treating uniform reconstruction as the final loss.
